segments.text: When you ask an AI a question, it first works out what your words mean together.
But once it understands the prompt, it faces an immediate challenge.
How exactly does it begin its reply?
Let's give the AI a simple question to track.
We'll ask, what should I name my new dog?
To make this easier to follow, we'll treat each whole word as a single token.
This diagram shows four steps before the answer begins.
Step one breaks the question into tokens.
Step two marks positions.
Step three creates starting vectors.
Step four runs numbers through layers for context.
Finally, AI uses the final token's updated numbers to predict what comes next.
In this graphic, the final token is the question mark.
It acts as a collector, gathering contextual information from every token before it,
transforming into its final vector numbers.
Those numbers act as a launchpad.
AI uses the final token's vector to predict the first token of its answer.
The AI is now ready to reply.
To find the very first word, it takes those updated numbers from the question mark
and calculates a probability score for every single potential token in its entire vocabulary.
This triggers a repeating generation loop.
The AI will select a top scoring token, add it to the reply,
and then use that newly expanded context window to run the prediction process all over again.
This chart breaks down the selection process step by step.
Let's look at prediction one on the left.
Because the reply hasn't started yet, the AI is solely using the question mark as its final
context token. The top predictions for this first slot are U at 18%, A at 14%, and Great at 9%.
In this instance, the AI selects U to start the sentence.
Following the arrow to the right, three subsequent prediction cycles occur.
The AI runs the loop repeatedly, smoothly adding the tokens could name and him to the sequence.
Arriving at prediction five in the top right, our context has now grown to read,
You could name him.
This means the word him acts as the new final token to launch the next prediction.
Based on this longer context, the top predictions shift significantly.
Down below, we see spot at 22%, max at 17%, and buddy at 14%.
The AI selects spot to complete the thought.
The completed sequence forms a full sentence.
You could name him spot.
You might notice a slight disconnect here.
We specifically asked for a dog name, yet the AI started its answer with the word you.
It did this because you is a highly probable, natural way to begin conversational text,
even before the specific subject of the dog is introduced.
Each added token changes what can fit next.
It is only after the sequence you could name him is established that a specific dog name
becomes the statistically obvious next choice.
The loop doesn't go on forever.
AI keeps predicting tokens until it produces a special token that signals the answer is finished.
This repeating cycle has a formal name, inference.
Let's look at this diagram to summarize exactly how it builds the answers step by step.
In step one, rank.
The AI scores every possible next token, just like we saw with the 22%, 17% and 14% probability scores
for dog names.
In step two, pick.
The AI makes a mathematical selection from those rankings, exactly as it picked spot.
Next is step three, add.
The selected token is physically attached to the growing answer sequence.
Finally, step four is repeat.
The AI takes this newly lengthened context and asks the model to predict all over again.
Pulling back, we can see the complete system.
Inference is the process AI uses to generate an answer one token at a time.
Every answer is built one token at a time.
The whole run is called inference.
